subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Prisoner's Dilemma: When Self-Interest Defeats Cooperation
description: A quick win: understand The Prisoner's Dilemma: When Self-Interest Defeats Cooperation.

hook.text: Two criminals are arrested. If both stay silent: light sentences.

buildup.text: The prisoner's dilemma: when individual rational self-interest leads to a collectively worse outcome.

discovery.text: Robert Axelrod's tournaments: in repeated games, the winning strategy isn't betrayal – it's 'tit for tat.' Start.

twist.text: Climate change, overfishing, & arms races are all real-world prisoner's dilemmas: everyone benefits from cooperation.

climax.text: The lesson: morality often IS the rational strategy – but only if the game is repeated & reputation matters.

punchline.text: In a one-time game, selfishness wins. In the game of life, cooperation does.

quiz.question: In Axelrod's repeated prisoner's dilemma tournaments, what was the winning strategy?
options: Tit for tat — start cooperating, then mirror the other player's moves

details.summary: The prisoner's dilemma shows how two rational individuals acting in self-interest produce a worse outcome than if they cooperated. It reveals a fundamental tension between individual rationality and collective benefit.
details.whyItMatters: The dilemma models real problems from arms races to climate change where mutual cooperation is better but hard to achieve.
takeaways: Individual rationality can lead to collective disaster
Trust and communication enable escape from the dilemma
Repeated interactions favor cooperative strategies like tit-for-tat

faq.question: Why do rational players end up with a worse outcome in the prisoner's dilemma?
faq.answer: Each player's best individual move is to defect regardless of the other's choice, but mutual defection produces a worse outcome than mutual cooperation.

faq.question: How does the prisoner's dilemma apply to climate change?
faq.answer: Nations benefit individually from polluting freely but collectively suffer from climate damage. Cooperation is optimal but difficult without enforcement mechanisms.
